purpose: Research recommendations for how ORYN's counselor/product logic should interpret secondary-education academic evidence across 8 systems. Conceptual research output only -- does not modify production schema or logic.
scope_note: 8 systems covered by design (not exhaustive): Turkiye/MEB, IB DP, AP, Cambridge IGCSE, Cambridge International AS & A Level, French Baccalaureat, German Abitur/DSD, US High School Diploma.
methodology_note: Each system researched independently by a dedicated research pass against primary/official sources (government ministries, IBO, College Board, Cambridge Assessment International Education, KMK) wherever fetchable; secondary sources used for discovery/corroboration only, never as sole evidence for a factual claim. Confidence and source_type are preserved per claim. See docs/research/secondary-education-systems/ for the full per-system narrative writeups this JSON also backs.

systems.system_name: Türkiye Ortaöğretim (Turkish Secondary Education under the Ministry of National Education / Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı, MEB) — Lise (grades 9-12)

A_identity.owner_authority: Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı (MEB, Turkish Ministry of National Education). The specific governing instrument for grades 9-12 is the 'Millî Eğitim Bakanlığı Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği' (MEB Secondary Education Institutions Regulation), issued under authority of the İlköğretim ve Eğitim Kanunu (Law 222), Millî Eğitim Temel Kanunu (Law 1739), and related statutes (Madde 1-3 of the regulation). Middle school (ortaokul, grades 5-8) is governed by a separate but structurally similar regulation, the İlköğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği, and is out of scope for ORYN's 'high_school' stage.
A_identity.contexts: Applies to all official (resmî) and private (özel) örgün (formal, in-person) secondary institutions affiliated with MEB inside Türkiye. Also applies, with adaptations, to MEB-affiliated schools for citizens abroad and to students returning from schooling abroad (Madde 66 governs re-entry grade conversion). Does not itself govern IB World Schools' IB Diploma track, Cambridge International tracks, or AP as administered by College Board — those are separate qualification frameworks that specific private schools layer on top of (or instead of) the MEB diploma track, authorized separately under Turkey's private-education statute (Law 5580, Özel Öğretim Kurumları Kanunu), not under the Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği itself.
A_identity.qualification_type: A national ministry-defined curriculum AND the diploma-granting framework combined: completing it via one of MEB's recognized school types (Fen Lisesi, Anadolu Lisesi, Sosyal Bilimler Lisesi, Güzel Sanatlar Lisesi, Spor Lisesi, Anadolu İmam Hatip Lisesi, Mesleki ve Teknik Anadolu Lisesi, Çok Programlı Anadolu Lisesi, Mesleki Eğitim Merkezi — Madde 6) results in an official 'Diploma' (commonly called Lise Diploması / Ortaöğretim Diploması) issued per Madde 69. It is best modeled as ORYN's curriculum='turkish_curriculum', not as a single 'exam' or narrow diploma type — it bundles a national course framework, an internal (school-administered, ministry-regulated) grading/promotion system, and a ministry-issued diploma, layered with entirely separate national placement exams (LGS, YKS) run by different bodies (MEB's own ÖDSGM for LGS; ÖSYM, an autonomous testing body, for YKS).
A_identity.notes: The regulation text used for this research is the version consolidated through amendments up to RG-22/2/2025-32821, retrieved from MEB's own tut.meb.gov.tr mirror. Article numbers cited below (Madde nn) refer to this regulation unless otherwise noted.

B_grading_model.native_form: Numerical, 0-100 point scale for every course score at every level (dönem puanı / term score, yılsonu puanı / course year-end score, yılsonu başarı puanı / overall year-end average, mezuniyet puanı or diploma notu / diploma score). There is NO 1-5 or letter-grade system in the current (post-2007) operative regulation for lise; a 5-point scale was used prior to 1 February 2007 and was formally abolished in favor of the 100-point system. (Some third-party sources describe a 1-5 scale as still relevant to Turkish schools generally — this appears to reflect either outdated information or possible confusion with an unrelated context; the primary regulation text extracted for this research contains no current 1-5 conversion for lise-level dönem/yılsonu/mezuniyet puanı. ORYN should treat any 1-5 description of the CURRENT lise system as unverified/likely stale.)
B_grading_model.scale_description: 0-100 for every score at every level. Course-level year-end score (yılsonu puanı, Madde 53) = arithmetic mean of the two term scores (dönem puanı, one per semester, Madde 51-53), each term score itself an arithmetic mean of exam scores + performance-task scores + project score (where applicable). The overall year-end average (yılsonu başarı puanı, Madde 54-55) is a WEIGHTED average across all of that year's courses, weighted by each course's weekly instructional-hour count ('ağırlık' = haftalık ders saati — i.e., credit-hour weighting, not a simple unweighted mean). The diploma score (mezuniyet puanı, Madde 65) is the unweighted arithmetic mean of the four yearly yılsonu başarı puanı values (9th, 10th, 11th, 12th grade), calculated to four decimal places. Passing threshold for an individual course (Madde 56): either (a) the arithmetic mean of the two term scores is at least 50, OR (b) regardless of the first term score, the second term score is at least 70. This 50-point threshold at lise level applies uniformly across subjects (no separate elevated Turkish-language threshold at lise level in the current text — that elevated Turkish-language threshold, 70 vs 50 for other subjects, is documented for ORTAOKUL/middle-school under a 2023-2024 regulation change, a DIFFERENT regulation than the one governing lise; ORYN should not assume it applies to high-school records). Grade promotion (sınıf geçme, Madde 57-59): 'doğrudan geçme' (direct pass) if failing at most 1 course and yılsonu başarı puanı ≥ 50; 'sorumlu geçme' (conditional pass with makeup-exam obligation) if yılsonu başarı puanı ≥ 50 and failing 2-3 courses (cumulative unresolved failed courses across grade levels capped at 6); otherwise 'sınıf tekrarı' (repeating the grade), which is capped at one repetition across the whole secondary program (prep year excluded from this cap, and has its own separate 2-year cap per Madde 60).
B_grading_model.official_conversions_found: 1) The MEB regulation itself defines a NARROW, single-purpose conversion but only in the OPPOSITE direction from what ORYN would typically need: Madde 66 tells schools how to convert grades EARNED ABROAD into the Turkish 100-point scale for a student re-entering Turkish schooling after partial study overseas — '5'li sistemde, her bir nota 1.00 eklenip, çıkan sayı elliyle çarpılıp üçe bölünerek puana çevrilir' (5-point foreign system: add 1.00 to the grade, multiply by 50, divide by 3) and '10'lu sistemde, her bir not 10 rakamıyla çarpılarak puana çevrilir' (10-point foreign system: multiply by 10). This is official but (a) converts INTO the Turkish scale, not out of it, and (b) exists solely for the narrow purpose of re-enrolling a returning student — it is not a general MEB-to-foreign-GPA conversion and should not be treated as one. 2) No official MEB-published conversion of the Turkish 100-point diploma notu to a foreign 4.0/5.0/10.0 GPA scale was found. 3) UK ENIC (the UK's official qualification-recognition body) explicitly states its Statement of Comparability service compares QUALIFICATION LEVEL only (it places the Devlet Lise Diploması roughly between GCSE and A-Level) and does NOT comment on grade-to-grade comparability at all — i.e., the UK's own official recognition body declines to certify a grade conversion. 4) The one clear example of an authoritative, source-published, purpose-specific conversion found is a single foreign university's own admissions page: University of Leeds Business School's international-qualifications equivalency page states, for its own direct-entry undergraduate admission purposes only: an overall grade of 85% in the final year (with at least 70% in Mathematics, or 85% for a higher-tier equivalence) is treated as comparable to AAA at A-Level, and 80% overall (same Mathematics condition) as comparable to AAB — explicitly restricted to applicants from Leeds-approved schools and to Leeds's own admissions decision. This is exactly the narrow, authoritative, purpose-bound exception the research brief allows citing — it must never be generalized into a universal MEB->GPA formula, and the original 100-point evidence should still be retained verbatim alongside any such note. 5) Generic 'Turkey to 4.0 GPA' conversion tables found on sites like gpacalculator.net and studyinturkiye.com are NOT authoritative (no named issuing institution, no stated purpose/scope) and must not be used as a basis for any ORYN conversion.

concepts: ders (course) — the atomic unit; each has a weekly-hour allocation ('haftalık ders saati') that doubles as its weighting/credit factor
dönem puanı (term/semester score) — per course, per semester (two per year); computed as the arithmetic mean of exam scores, performance-task score(s), and project score where applicable (Madde 51)
yılsonu puanı (course year-end score) — per course, per year; arithmetic mean of the two dönem puanı values (Madde 53)
ağırlıklı puan (weighted score) — a course's yılsonu puanı multiplied by its weekly-hour weight (Madde 54)

yılsonu başarı puanı (year-end success/overall average) — sum of all courses' weighted scores divided by the sum of all courses' weekly hours; i.e., an hours-weighted GPA-equivalent for that single school year (Madde 55)

mezuniyet puanı / diploma notu (diploma score) — arithmetic mean of the four yearly yılsonu başarı puanı values (9th-12th grade), computed to 4 decimal places, printed on the diploma as 'Diploma Puanı' (Madde 65, Madde 69)

sınıf geçme (grade promotion) — doğrudan geçme (direct pass), sorumlu geçme (conditional pass owing makeup exams for up to 3 failed courses), sınıf tekrarı (repeating the year, capped at once in the whole secondary program excluding prep year) (Madde 56-59)
sorumluluk sınavı (makeup/responsibility exam) — exam a student in 'sorumlu geçme' status must pass (≥50) to clear an outstanding failed course (Madde 58)

hazırlık sınıfı (preparation/prep year) — an optional pre-9th-grade year at specific ministry-approved, centrally-exam-admitted schools, focused on intensive foreign-language instruction; passed via a proficiency exam (yeterlilik sınavı) in the first foreign language and in 'Hazırlık Sınıfı Türk Dili ve Edebiyatı'; grades earned during hazırlık sınıfı are explicitly EXCLUDED from the mezuniyet puanı calculation (Madde 60(1): 'Hazırlık sınıfında alınan puanlar mezuniyet puanının belirlenmesinde dikkate alınmaz')

e-Okul — the central MEB electronic student-information system of record; all of the above scores, the okul birincisi designation, and diploma data are recorded here and it is the operational source of a Turkish transcript/karne

öğrenci gelişim dosyası (student development file) — a separate MEB-defined electronic portfolio record (Madde 4) tracking a student's interests/talents/skills through in-school and out-of-school activities, national/international project participation, and social-responsibility-program hours; distinct from the academic grade record, closer in spirit to ORYN's evidence/portfolio concept than to GPA

ortak dersler / alan-dal dersleri / seçmeli dersler — common (core) courses, field/branch (vocational-track) courses, and elective courses respectively — the three official course categories that make up a school's haftalık ders çizelgesi (weekly course schedule)
C_structure_concepts.explanation: All of these concepts apply uniformly to every MEB-affiliated lise (grades 9-12), regardless of school type, EXCEPT hazırlık sınıfı, which only exists at schools the Ministry has approved to offer a prep year (typically foreign-language-intensive, centrally-exam-admitted schools per Madde 6(3)) — most Turkish high schools have no hazırlık sınıfı at all.

sources.note: Madde 4 (definitions), Madde 6 (school types/prep year authorization), Madde 50-60 (course scoring and promotion mechanics), Madde 65 (diploma score), Madde 69 (diploma content fields) — all directly quoted/paraphrased from the extracted regulation text.

signals: School type / admission mechanism: Fen Lisesi (science high school), Sosyal Bilimler Lisesi (social-sciences high school), and specific Anadolu Lisesi / Anadolu Teknik programs are admitted via LGS, a competitive central placement exam — factually more selective at the point of entry than schools with no entrance exam. Standard Anadolu Lisesi (the largest category) and other lise types generally do not use LGS-based competitive placement in the same way, or use it with much lower cutoffs; imam-hatip, mesleki ve teknik (vocational/technical), and çok programlı schools serve different populations and purposes. ORYN should treat 'which admission mechanism this specific school used' as a factual, retrievable signal (from ORYN's own school registry), not a score it invents.

hazırlık sınıfı presence — only certain Ministry-approved, typically foreign-language-intensive schools offer a prep year; its presence is a factual attribute of the specific school/program, and (per Madde 60) its grades never enter the diploma-score calculation — it is evidence of extra foreign-language exposure, not evidence of stronger/weaker academic performance in the diploma-bearing years.

alan/dal (field/branch) structure — vocational and technical Anadolu lisesi students split into alan/dal tracks with a different course mix (more applied/occupational courses, staj/işletmede beceri eğitimi — workplace internship components) than general Anadolu/Fen/Sosyal Bilimler lisesi students; this is a structural, factual difference in what was actually studied, not a rigor ranking.

seçmeli ders (elective course) load and choice — the specific electives a school offers and a student selects (Madde 50) is a factual, school-dependent signal of what was actually available and chosen; the same nominal course title can differ in rigor between schools, so elective choice should always be read against what that specific school offered, never against a generic national norm.

Foreign qualifications layered at the same school (AP, IB, A-Level/Cambridge) — the MEB regulation itself is completely silent on these (a full-text search of the 106-page regulation for 'AP', 'International Baccalaureate', 'A-Level', 'Cambridge' returned zero matches); where a specific Turkish school offers these, they exist as a separate, privately-arranged academic track/exam layered on top of (or alongside) the MEB diploma, authorized under Turkey's separate private-education statute, not under the Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği. Their presence or absence at a given school is a fact about that specific school (already tracked in ORYN's Turkey school registry per the task brief), never something to assume uniformly across 'Turkish private schools' as a class.
D_rigor_signals.explanation: None of these are official MEB 'rigor scores' — MEB does not publish or imply any such ranking of school types or course loads. They are simply real, verifiable structural facts a counselor could use to contextualize a transcript (e.g., 'this student attended a LGS-admitted Fen Lisesi with no AP/IB program' vs. 'this student attended a standard Anadolu Lisesi that also offers 6 AP courses'), and ORYN should surface them as facts, not fold them into a synthetic score.

sources.note: Madde 6 (school types and hazırlık sınıfı authorization), Madde 50 (elective/project/performance-task obligations), Madde 60 (hazırlık sınıfı exclusion from diploma score); also the direct full-text search confirming zero mentions of AP/IB/A-Level/Cambridge in this regulation.

WES (World Education Services) descriptive overview corroborating Fen Lisesi and Anadolu Lisesi as more academically selective tracks; used for discovery/context only — note this WES article is dated 2017 and uses the pre-2018 exam names (YGS/LYS), so it should not be relied on for current exam-system details (see section G).

E_predicted_grades.status: No formal MEB-defined 'predicted grade' concept exists, unlike IB's official Predicted Grade construct. This is confirmed by absence: the 106-page Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği defines only actually-earned scores (dönem puanı, yılsonu puanı, yılsonu başarı puanı, mezuniyet puanı) — there is no ministry-defined mechanism for a teacher or school to issue a forward-looking projected final grade with any official status.
E_predicted_grades.explanation: What actually happens in practice when a Turkish student applies to universities abroad while still in 12th grade (this part is NOT verified against an authoritative/official source — it reflects general international-admissions-counseling practice described by secondary sources, e.g. general guidance about 'curriculum in progress' transcripts on platforms like the Common App, and international-transcript-evaluation consultancy pages): the student typically submits official transcripts for completed years (grades 9-11 finalized, i.e., official yılsonu puanı/yılsonu başarı puanı data) plus whatever of the current (12th) year is available at application time (typically first-semester dönem puanı values, since the full-year yılsonu puanı for 12th grade isn't finalized until the school year ends). Some receiving universities/counselors informally ask the school counselor for a qualitative or numeric estimate of expected final performance, but this is an ad hoc school-counselor communication, not a ministry-recognized, standardized document the way an IB Predicted Grade is. ORYN should represent a MEB student's senior year as 'in-progress official data through the most recent completed term' rather than inventing or requesting a 'predicted grade' field, and should never treat an informal counselor estimate as equivalent in authority to a finalized MEB yılsonu puanı.

sources.note: Negative evidence: full regulation contains no predicted-grade mechanism, only actually-earned dönem/yılsonu/mezuniyet puanı definitions.

General (non-Turkey-specific, non-official) description of how 'curriculum in progress' international transcripts are typically handled for US admissions — used for discovery/context only, not as sole evidence; the specific Turkey-context claims in this section should be treated as informed inference, not a verified MEB or university-published fact.

F_class_rank.status: Not a structural part of an individual MEB student's record. Class rank / percentile is NOT computed, stored, or printed for every student. The only rank-like construct in the regulation is 'okul birincisi' (school top student / valedictorian) — a single title awarded to exactly one student per school (or one per specialized program at schools with multiple diploma programs, e.g. separate okul birincisi for each Anadolu meslek/teknik program) at the point of graduation, determined by the teachers' council based on highest 4-year mezuniyet puanı, with a defined tie-breaking cascade (Madde 64) ending in a lottery draw if all else is tied. This is an end-of-program administrative honor, not a running per-student rank, and it is NOT one of the fields printed on the diploma itself (Madde 69(3)(a) enumerates the diploma's fields exhaustively — T.C. Kimlik No, name, parents' names, birth place/date, issuing school, school/diploma numbers, foreign language, Diploma Puanı, diploma date, öğrenim süresi, security number, program/alan-dal — no rank field appears in that list).
F_class_rank.explanation: For the vast majority of MEB students (everyone except the single per-school/per-program okul birincisi), no numeric or percentile class rank exists anywhere in their official record. ORYN's rule to never infer class rank when absent is exactly correct for MEB records — rank is not just 'often missing,' it is structurally absent by design for essentially all students, and even where 'okul birincisi' is self-reported by a top student, it should be treated as a specific named honor (verifiable via evidence/e-Okul-derived documentation) rather than as a generic 'class rank' data point, and never used to back-infer a rank for any other student at that school.

sources.note: Madde 64 (Okul birincilerinin tespiti — full determination and tie-break procedure) and Madde 69(3)(a) (exhaustive list of diploma fields, no rank field) directly extracted and confirmed from the regulation text.

outputs: LGS (Liselere Geçiş Sistemi kapsamındaki merkezî sınav) — a centralized placement exam for 8th-grade (ortaokul) students seeking admission to selective high-school programs (Fen Lisesi, Sosyal Bilimler Lisesi, project schools, Anadolu Teknik programs). Administered by MEB's own Ölçme, Değerlendirme ve Sınav Hizmetleri Genel Müdürlüğü (ÖDSGM) — i.e., this IS an MEB-run exam, not an outside body. Sitting LGS is NOT mandatory ('Öğrencilerin merkezî sınava girme zorunluluğu bulunmuyor'). It occurs BEFORE high school begins and functions as a placement/admission signal for which lise the student attends, not as part of the lise-level academic transcript itself.

YKS (Yükseköğretim Kurumları Sınavı) — Turkey's national university-entrance exam, composed of TYT (Temel Yeterlilik Testi, basic competency test) and, for those seeking placement in more specialized programs, AYT (Alan Yeterlilik Testi, field-competency test) and/or YDT (Yabancı Dil Testi, foreign-language test for language-based programs). Administered by ÖSYM (Ölçme, Seçme ve Yerleştirme Merkezi), an autonomous state testing authority under YÖK (the Higher Education Council) — a DIFFERENT body from MEB, even though it operates on MEB-curriculum content. Taken near the end of/after 12th grade. A portion of the diploma notu is folded into the YKS placement score via OBP (Ortaöğretim Başarı Puanı): diploma notu (0-100) is scaled to a 250-500 range (commonly described as diploma notu × 5), and OBP × a fixed ÖSYM coefficient (widely reported as 0.12) is added to the candidate's raw YKS score. NOTE: the exact OBP formula and 0.12 coefficient were corroborated across multiple secondary/consultant sources (a Turkish private university's own admissions blog, several exam-prep calculator sites) but were NOT independently verified against ÖSYM's own official YKS kılavuzu (guide) PDF in this research pass — flagged as medium confidence, not primary-source-verified.

AP / IB / A-Level / SAT and similar — these are entirely separate from LGS/YKS. They are foreign qualifications/exams that specific Turkish schools additionally offer (per ORYN's own Turkey school registry), sat through College Board, IBO, or Cambridge Assessment International Education respectively, and are unrelated to MEB's own grading, promotion, or diploma-scoring regulation. A Turkish student can hold both a MEB Lise Diploması (with its LGS/YKS history) AND AP/IB/A-Level results from the same school — these must be modeled and reasoned about as distinct, parallel data, never merged or treated as substitutes for one another.
G_external_assessment.explanation: LGS and YKS/TYT/AYT/YDT are Turkey's own national-system standardized assessments (LGS run directly by MEB; YKS run by the separate ÖSYM body but built on MEB curriculum content) and should be modeled in ORYN's generic test_scores table (test_name='LGS' / 'YKS-TYT' / 'YKS-AYT' etc., with subscores jsonb capturing per-section net/puan breakdowns where available). AP/IB/A-Level/SAT taken by the same student are separate rows in the same test_scores table but conceptually and administratively unrelated to LGS/YKS — ORYN's advisor logic should never conflate 'this student's LGS/YKS performance' with 'this student's AP/IB performance' when reasoning about academic strength, since they measure different things for different purposes (domestic placement vs. often foreign-university-facing credentials).

sources.note: MEB ÖDSGM's own official page describing the Liselere Geçiş Sistemi (LGS) — confirms it is MEB-run, confirms non-mandatory status and purpose (placement into Fen Lisesi/Sosyal Bilimler Lisesi/project schools/Anadolu Teknik programs).

Işık Üniversitesi (a Turkish private university)'s own admissions-office blog explaining OBP calculation and the 0.12 coefficient — a reputable but non-ÖSYM-primary source; corroborated by several independent exam-prep calculator sites but not independently checked against ÖSYM's own kılavuzu in this pass.

H_unsafe_inferences: Do not compute or display a class rank (numeric or percentile) for a MEB student — it is not part of the official record for any student except the single, separately-designated 'okul birincisi' per school/program, and even that is an end-of-program honor, not a running rank.

Do not convert a MEB 100-point diploma notu / yılsonu başarı puanı / dönem puanı into a US 4.0 (or any other) GPA scale by default. No universal official conversion exists. The only legitimate exception is quoting a SPECIFIC named institution's own published, purpose-bound conversion (e.g., 'University of Leeds treats an 85% final-year average as AAA-equivalent for its own direct-entry undergraduate admissions') — and even then, the original 100-point figure must be retained and displayed alongside, never replaced by the converted figure.

Do not use the Madde 66 foreign-grade-into-Turkish-scale formula (for students returning from abroad) in reverse, or for any purpose other than the narrow one it was written for (re-enrolling a returning student in a Turkish school).

Do not assume every Turkish school (even elite/well-known private schools) offers AP, IB, or A-Level — MEB's own regulation never mentions these, confirming they are school-specific, privately-arranged add-ons; always check the specific school's actual offerings (ORYN's Turkey school registry) rather than inferring from school reputation or type.

Do not assume a hazırlık sınıfı (prep year) exists for a given school/student unless explicitly recorded — it exists only at Ministry-approved, typically centrally-exam-admitted schools, and even where it exists, do not fold its grades into the diploma-score average — MEB explicitly excludes them (Madde 60(1)).

Do not treat a lower MEB numeric average (e.g., 65/100) as inherently 'weak' or a higher one (e.g., 95/100) as inherently 'strong' without considering the issuing school's own grading norms and course difficulty — MEB scoring is locally administered by each school's own teachers within ministry-defined mechanics, so absolute numbers are not nationally curve-normalized or directly comparable across schools without more context.

Do not compute or estimate a Turkish student's LGS or YKS/TYT/AYT score, or infer one from course grades — these are independently administered, separately scored exams (LGS by MEB/ÖDSGM, YKS by ÖSYM) with their own separate data pipeline; only report scores the student actually supplied.

Do not treat AP/IB/A-Level exam results taken at a Turkish school as part of, or a substitute for, that student's MEB dönem/yılsonu/mezuniyet puanı, or vice versa — they are parallel, non-fungible records.

Do not fabricate or assume an IB-style 'predicted grade' for a MEB student — no such ministry-recognized construct exists; only report actually-finalized dönem/yılsonu puanı values, clearly labeled by which term/year they cover, plus explicit 'in progress' labeling for anything not yet finalized.

Do not assume the ortaokul (middle-school) passing-threshold change (Turkish 70 / other courses 50, effective 2023-2024) applies to lise (high school) records — the lise-level threshold documented directly from the regulation is a uniform 50 across subjects (Madde 56), from a different regulation instrument than the one governing ortaokul.

should_care_about: The trend across the four yearly yılsonu başarı puanı values (9th through 12th grade, or through whatever years are complete) — improving, flat, or declining trajectory on the student's own 100-point scale, read in the student's own school context, not against a converted GPA.

What courses/electives/alan-dal track the student actually took relative to what their SPECIFIC school offered (seçmeli ders choices, alan/dal track for vocational students, any AP/IB/A-Level courses layered on at that particular school) — rigor should be read relative to the real options available at that school, never against a generic national norm.

Whether the school is one that required competitive admission (e.g., LGS-admitted Fen Lisesi/Sosyal Bilimler Lisesi/Anadolu Teknik program) versus one that did not — a factual, retrievable attribute of the specific school, useful context for interpreting the record but not a multiplier applied to the grades themselves.

Performance on LGS (if available, as context for how the student arrived at their current high school) and on YKS/TYT/AYT (as the actual, MEB-independent standardized outcome that matters for Turkish university placement) — reported and reasoned about separately from course grades, never blended into a single number.

Any AP/IB/A-Level/SAT results the student has from the same or another school, reasoned about as independent evidence relevant primarily to foreign-university applications, not as a re-scoring of the MEB record.

Whether a hazırlık sınıfı year exists in the record, and if so, treating it explicitly as extra (mainly language) preparation time excluded from the diploma score by ministry rule — not as a 'wasted' or 'bonus' year to editorialize about.
Self-reported honors like 'okul birincisi' (school valedictorian), always flagged as self-reported pending evidence, and never auto-inferred for any student who hasn't explicitly reported it.
should_not_care_about: Any fabricated or default-converted GPA/4.0 figure for a MEB student.
Any invented percentile or class rank for students other than a self-reported, evidence-pending 'okul birincisi.'
Generic assumptions like 'this student went to a well-known private school, so they must have taken AP/IB' — verify against the actual school registry data instead.
Treating LGS/YKS scores as if they were course grades, or treating course grades as a proxy for LGS/YKS performance.

Any assumption that a student's numeric average is comparable, without adjustment, to a student's numeric average from a different Turkish school — MEB scoring is not centrally curve-normalized across schools.

J_profile_data_model_implications.fits_existing_schema_how: A standard MEB-only lise enrollment (grades 9-12, no prep year, no foreign qualifications) fits cleanly into ONE education_records row: curriculum='turkish_curriculum', stage='high_school', overall_gpa = the diploma notu / mezuniyet puanı (or the latest available yılsonu başarı puanı if the student hasn't graduated yet) stored as a plain 0-100 number, gpa_scale=100. Each course maps to a courses row with level='regular' (level='dual_enrollment'/'other' generally won't apply; 'honors' has no direct MEB equivalent — MEB does not have an official 'honors' course tier the way US systems do, so 'regular' is the correct default for standard MEB courses even when the school is a selective Fen Lisesi — selectivity lives at the SCHOOL level, not at the per-course level, in this system). grade_value (TEXT) should store the native 0-100 score exactly as recorded (e.g. '87', or '87.50' if MEB's four-decimal-place convention is preserved), grade_scale='100'. Where a student at a MEB school ALSO takes AP, IB (individual courses/exams, not a full IB Diploma Programme), or A-Level courses/exams, those individual courses map to the SAME education_record's courses rows but with level='ap' / 'ib_hl' / 'ib_sl' / 'a_level' as appropriate — this correctly represents the common Turkish pattern where the MEB diploma remains the primary credential and AP/IB/A-Level are supplementary exams layered on top at the same school, not a separate curriculum track. LGS, YKS-TYT, YKS-AYT, YKS-YDT, and any AP/IB/SAT scores all map to test_scores rows (test_name distinguishing each), which the generic schema already supports well with score/max_score as TEXT and subscores as jsonb for section-level breakdowns.
gaps: No field distinctly flags that a given overall_gpa value IS the ministry-defined 'diploma notu' (computed via the specific Madde 65 four-year-average formula) as opposed to a self-reported or partial-year average — recommend Claude B use the `notes` field on the education_records row to explicitly annotate this (e.g. 'MEB mezuniyet puanı — arithmetic mean of 9th-12th yılsonu başarı puanı per Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği Madde 65') so the advisor/UI can distinguish a ministry-computed figure from a self-entered estimate.

There is no entity for the MEB-specific intermediate rollup 'yılsonu başarı puanı' (the single hours-weighted average FOR ONE YEAR that feeds into the four-year diploma notu) — the schema has courses (per-course) and education_records (per-enrollment-period, presumably spanning all 4 years or split by year depending on how Claude B models multi-year enrollments), but no 'per-year summary score' entity. If education_records is modeled as ONE row per 4-year lise enrollment, the four separate yearly yılsonu başarı puanı values that mathematically produce the diploma notu have nowhere to live individually — only the final diploma notu fits into overall_gpa. Recommend Claude B either (a) accept this as an acceptable simplification (store only the final diploma notu, treat the yearly rollups as non-persisted intermediate data), or (b) if year-by-year academic trend matters to the advisor (plausible, since 'is this student's trajectory improving' is a real counselor question), consider modeling one education_records row PER GRADE-YEAR at the same school (all curriculum='turkish_curriculum', same school_name, sequential start_date/end_date) so each year's overall_gpa can hold that year's yılsonu başarı puanı — this is a genuine design choice for Claude B, not something this research prescribes.

No dedicated flag for hazırlık sınıfı (prep year) status. If modeled as its own education_records row (recommended, since it has its own start/end dates and its grades must NOT be pooled with the diploma-bearing years per Madde 60), the existing stage enum (middle_school|high_school|pre_university|undergraduate|other) has no exact match — 'pre_university' is the closest conceptual fit (it genuinely precedes the 9th-grade diploma track) but could be misread as referring to something else (e.g. a foundation year at a different level); Claude B should decide whether 'pre_university' is acceptable or whether a schema-level addition is eventually warranted — this research only flags the gap, it does not recommend a schema change.

No field for 'okul birincisi' (school valedictorian) status — this is a named honor/award, not a grade or course, so it likely belongs in ORYN's separate `awards` entity (referenced in the product spec's Phase 58 schema list) rather than anywhere in education_records/courses; flagging so Claude B applies the same self_reported -> evidence_added -> verified status pipeline to it as to any other award, and never auto-computes it.

No field for alan/dal (vocational field/branch) or the specific program type (e.g. 'Anadolu Lisesi' vs 'Fen Lisesi' vs 'Anadolu Teknik Programı') distinct from school_name/curriculum — this is more naturally sourced from ORYN's own Turkey school registry (which the task brief says already tracks per-school program offerings) than duplicated onto every student's education_records row; flagging as a linkage point rather than a schema gap in education_records itself.

test_scores' generic shape (test_name, score, max_score, subscores jsonb, test_date) comfortably accommodates LGS, YKS-TYT, YKS-AYT, YKS-YDT, and AP/IB/SAT results side by side with no gap identified.

matrix_row.curriculum_qualification_exam: MEB national curriculum + MEB-issued Lise Diploması (Ortaöğretim Diploması); separately, LGS (MEB/ÖDSGM, high-school placement, pre-lise) and YKS/TYT/AYT/YDT (ÖSYM, university placement, end of lise) as distinct national standardized exams; AP/IB/A-Level exist only where a specific school layers them on separately.
matrix_row.native_grading_scale: 0-100 numeric at every level (term/dönem puanı, course year-end/yılsonu puanı, annual overall/yılsonu başarı puanı, 4-year diploma/mezuniyet puanı); passing threshold at lise level = 50 (or second-term score ≥70 regardless of first term), per Madde 56.
matrix_row.external_exam: LGS (MEB-run, optional, pre-high-school placement) and YKS = TYT + AYT (+YDT for language programs) (ÖSYM-run, university entrance); OBP folds diploma notu into the YKS score at a reported 0.12 coefficient (medium-confidence, not primary-source-verified in this pass). Distinct from any AP/IB/SAT a student may also hold from a specific school.
matrix_row.predicted_grades: No formal MEB predicted-grade construct exists (confirmed by absence in the regulation). In practice, applications made during 12th grade rely on finalized 9th-11th grade data plus whatever of 12th grade's first-semester dönem puanı is available, not a standardized predicted-grade document — this practice detail is not independently verified against an authoritative source and should be treated as informed context, not fact.
matrix_row.course_levels: MEB courses default to ORYN's level='regular' (MEB itself has no honors/AP-equivalent internal tier — selectivity is a school-level, not course-level, attribute). AP/IB_HL/IB_SL/A-Level courses taken at the same school map to their respective ORYN level enum values as supplementary courses within the same education_record.
matrix_row.class_rank_inherent: No — structurally absent for essentially all students. The only exception is 'okul birincisi,' a single per-school (or per-program) end-of-program honor determined by the teachers' council, not a running rank, and not printed on the diploma itself.
matrix_row.safe_gpa_conversion: None found from MEB or from any general/universal authority; UK ENIC explicitly declines to certify grade-level comparability. The only defensible example is a NAMED foreign university's own narrow-purpose table (e.g., University of Leeds Business School's 85%/80% final-year-average thresholds for its own direct-entry admissions) — cite by name and purpose only, never generalize, and always retain the original 100-point figure.
matrix_row.important_oryn_interpretation: Read the diploma notu / yılsonu başarı puanı trend on its own 100-point scale, in the context of the specific school's own selectivity/admission mechanism and actual course/elective/AP-IB offerings (per ORYN's school registry); treat LGS and YKS as separate, MEB/ÖSYM-owned data points, not derivable from course grades; never invent a class rank, a converted GPA, a predicted grade, or an assumed AP/IB/hazırlık-sınıfı status.

unresolved_questions: The exact current OBP-to-YKS coefficient (widely reported as 0.12) was corroborated only via secondary/consultant sources (a Turkish private university's admissions blog and exam-prep calculator sites), not verified directly against ÖSYM's own official YKS Kılavuzu (guide) PDF for the current admissions cycle — should be independently confirmed against ÖSYM's own publication before being surfaced to users as a precise figure.

Whether the lise-level uniform 50-point passing threshold (Madde 56, from the Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği extracted here) has since been amended to differentiate by subject (mirroring the 2023-2024 ortaokul-level Turkish-language-70/other-50 change) was not found in the consolidated regulation text through the 22/2/2025 amendment used here — treated as still-uniform-at-50 based on the most recent official text found, but a newer amendment (post the version retrieved) cannot be ruled out.

The precise, real-world frequency and format of any informal 'predicted grade' or counselor estimate that Turkish schools provide to foreign universities for in-progress 12th-grade applicants was not verified against any official or school-specific source — flagged in section E as informed context only, not fact.

Whether any additional MEB circular/yönerge (directive, a lower tier of MEB rule-making than a full yönetmelik/regulation) further modifies dönem/yılsonu puanı mechanics for specific school types (e.g., Fen Lisesi-specific or Sosyal Bilimler Lisesi-specific circulars) was not investigated — this research covers the general Ortaöğretim Kurumları Yönetmeliği only, as that is the primary regulatory instrument, but school-type-specific circulars could in principle add nuance not captured here.

Whether Türkiye has any IB World Schools where the IB Diploma Programme itself (not just individual AP/IB courses) is the primary diploma-granting credential (which would argue for curriculum='ib' rather than 'turkish_curriculum' for that specific education_record) was not investigated in this pass — this is a per-school fact ORYN's existing Turkey school registry should already resolve, not something this system-level research can generalize about.

A_identity.owner_authority: International Baccalaureate Organization (IBO / trades as 'International Baccalaureate' or 'IB'), a non-profit foundation headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, founded 1968.
A_identity.countries_contexts: Global. Offered only at authorized 'IB World Schools.' Per ibo.org 'Facts and figures' (search-snippet, as surfaced ~Aug 2026): IB programmes are offered across 6,200+ schools in 160+ countries; DP is specifically for students aged approximately 16-19, typically the final two years of secondary school.
A_identity.qualification_type: Two genuinely distinct outcomes exist under the same DP curriculum umbrella, and ORYN must not collapse them: (1) the full 'IB Diploma' -- a diploma awarded only when a candidate completes all six subjects plus TOK, EE, and CAS and meets the passing conditions in section B; (2) 'IB Diploma Programme courses' (sometimes called IB course candidates, historically 'IB Certificate') -- a track where a student takes one or more individual DP subjects and sits the subject assessment(s) for IB course results/certificates, WITHOUT completing TOK/EE/CAS and WITHOUT the overall Diploma being awarded. A student can therefore have IB HL/SL subject grades on record without ever having pursued or earned the Diploma itself. This is a precise, source-grounded distinction (not an ORYN assumption) and is directly relevant to the schema question in section J.

B_grading_model.subject_scale: Each of the 6 subjects (both HL and SL -- HL/SL affects depth/content, not the grading scale) is graded on a 1-7 scale, 7 highest.
B_grading_model.core_points: Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and the Extended Essay (EE) are each graded separately on an A-E letter scale, then combined via an official IBO points matrix into 0-3 bonus 'core points' added to the diploma total. Example combination reported via search-snippet (NOT independently verified against the raw current matrix table): 'a candidate who receives a B in TOK and a C in the EE will be awarded 2 points.' The exact current full matrix (all A-E x A-E combinations) could not be retrieved verbatim this session -- treat as unresolved/needs direct verification, see unresolved_questions.
B_grading_model.diploma_total: Maximum 45 points = 42 (6 subjects x 7 max) + 3 (TOK/EE core points). This total is a bounded composite score with its own IBO-defined pass/fail logic -- it is NOT a GPA and has no official GPA-scale equivalence.
B_grading_model.passing_award_conditions: Per the official ibo.org 'DP passing criteria' page (search-snippet extraction, medium-high confidence, not independently re-verified verbatim): the Diploma is awarded only if ALL of the following hold: (1) total >= 24 points; (2) NO grade E in TOK or EE (an E in either is an automatic failing condition regardless of total score); (3) at least grade 2 in every subject (no subject grade below 2); (4) no more than two grade 2s awarded; (5) no more than three grade 3s-or-below awarded; (6) at least 12 points combined across HL subjects; (7) at least 9 points combined across SL subjects; (8) a grade has been awarded in every subject, TOK, and EE (nothing missing/incomplete); (9) CAS has been completed and certified by the school (CAS is pass/fail, not graded -- see C).
B_grading_model.gpa_conversion_rule: No universal IB-to-GPA/4.0 conversion exists or should be invented. Grade boundaries (the raw-mark-to-1-7-grade cutoffs) are reset by IBO after every May/November session, per subject, per level, and sometimes per exam variant -- there is no fixed percentage table. Any GPA-equivalence table in circulation is, at most, an individual receiving UNIVERSITY's own published admissions policy (e.g. a specific US university choosing to map IB HL 6/7 to its own 4.0 scale for internal use) and must be stored/labeled as that institution's own policy if ever used, never as a universal IB rule.

C_structure_concepts.subject: One of 6 subjects; the candidate takes one subject from each of Groups 1-5 plus a sixth subject from Group 6 (the arts) OR, per IB flexibility rules, a second subject from Groups 1-5 in place of a Group 6 arts subject. (This substitution-flexibility claim is corroborated by multiple secondary sources but was NOT independently confirmed against a raw ibo.org fetch this session -- flag as medium confidence, see unresolved_questions.)
C_structure_concepts.hl_vs_sl: At least 3 and not more than 4 of the 6 subjects are taken at Higher Level (HL); the remainder at Standard Level (SL). Both HL and SL use the same 1-7 grade scale -- the level affects instructional depth/hours, not the scale itself. (Commonly-cited HL ~240 teaching hours vs SL ~150 teaching hours over the 2-year programme was surfaced in this research but is a widely-repeated secondary figure, not independently confirmed against a raw ibo.org fetch this session -- flag as medium confidence.)
C_structure_concepts.tok: Theory of Knowledge -- a required core element, distinct from the 6 subjects, graded A-E, contributes to core points, not a 'subject' in the group sense.
C_structure_concepts.ee: Extended Essay -- required independent research essay (~4000 words), distinct from the 6 subjects, graded A-E, contributes to core points.
C_structure_concepts.cas: Creativity, Activity, Service -- required core element, NOT graded at all (no letter or number grade). Assessed as complete/incomplete by the school's CAS coordinator against 7 IBO-defined learning outcomes and student reflections/evidence. Diploma is withheld if CAS is not satisfactorily completed, independent of subject/TOK/EE performance.
C_structure_concepts.predicted_grade: A teacher-assigned, pre-final-exam ESTIMATE (1-7 per subject) of the grade a candidate is expected to achieve, based on internal assessments, mock exams, coursework, and professional judgment. Submitted by the SCHOOL (not the student) to IBO/onward to universities. Genuinely separate data point from the final grade -- see E.
C_structure_concepts.final_examination_result: The actual 1-7 grade per subject, released after the May or November exam session, derived from externally-set and/or externally-moderated assessment components (see G).
C_structure_concepts.ib_diploma_total: The summed, IBO-computed 0-45 total across the 6 subject grades plus core points -- a DERIVED aggregate, not itself one subject's grade, and not a GPA.
C_structure_concepts.product_rule: ORYN must keep subject grade (1-7), TOK grade (A-E), EE grade (A-E), CAS completion status, predicted grade, final grade, and diploma total as six/seven SEPARATE concepts -- never flatten into one number.

D_rigor_signals.hl_sl_distinction: Number and identity of HL vs SL subjects (3-4 HL out of 6) is a factual rigor signal ORYN can surface as-is -- do not compress into a synthetic score.
D_rigor_signals.six_subject_group_flexibility: Some flexibility exists in substituting a second Groups-1-5 subject for the Group 6 arts subject (medium confidence, not independently re-verified verbatim this session -- see unresolved_questions).
D_rigor_signals.instruction: ORYN should report which subjects were taken at which level and let the counselor/AI-advisor layer interpret relevance to the student's target field (e.g. HL Economics + HL Math relevant to an Economics target) -- do not invent a numeric 'rigor score' for IB itself; that belongs to ORYN's own scoring engine (Phase 6 of the build spec), fed by these facts, not baked into the research layer.

E_predicted_grades.existence: Predicted grades formally exist and are a real, named part of the IB process (distinct from a generic 'teacher estimate').
E_predicted_grades.mechanism: Set by the school/teachers using professional judgment informed by internal assessments, mock exam results, coursework quality, and classroom performance. IBO does not prescribe one fixed calculation formula -- this is corroborated across many secondary sources but the exact IBO-side procedural language was not independently confirmed via a raw ibo.org fetch this session.
E_predicted_grades.university_use: Used directly in university admissions before final results exist. UK: the school submits predicted grades, which flow to UCAS and are used by universities to make conditional offers ahead of the July results. UCAS's own guidance (search-snippet extraction, direct fetch blocked with HTTP 403) states predicted grades 'should be set independently of an applicant's university or college choices' and be 'objective and data-driven ... determined by professional judgement' -- and explicitly that the final admissions decision is made only once ACHIEVED (final) results are received, i.e. predicted grades are not a guarantee.
E_predicted_grades.timing_caveat: Secondary sources report predicted grades are typically finalized in the DP2 (final) year, in a window roughly September-January depending on school and target deadline (e.g. UK Oxbridge/medicine applications need predictions finalized earlier, around mid-October, vs end-January for most other UK courses). This timing/window detail is secondary-corroborated only -- NOT independently confirmed against a primary IBO or UCAS document this session. Flag as medium confidence.
E_predicted_grades.distinct_from_final: Predicted grade != final grade. ORYN must never treat a predicted grade as equivalent to, or a reliable proxy for, the final examination result.

F_class_rank.finding: IBO does not compute, define, or publish class rank as part of the DP. Whether a given IB World School reports class rank to universities is entirely a SCHOOL or national-system policy choice, independent of the IB curriculum itself (many schools that run IB explicitly do not rank). ORYN must never infer or derive a class rank from 1-7 subject grades or the diploma point total.

G_external_assessment.structure: Final subject grades derive from a mix of externally-set/externally-marked written examinations AND, for many subjects, internally-assessed components (e.g. Internal Assessments, oral components) that are marked by the student's own teacher and then externally MODERATED (sample-checked and adjusted) by IBO examiners. So 'IB assessment' is not uniformly '100% one external exam per subject' -- it is externally controlled/moderated end-to-end, but the balance of internal vs external marking varies by subject.
G_external_assessment.sessions: Two exam sessions per year: May (dominant, aligned to Northern Hemisphere school calendars) and November (Southern Hemisphere and some schools). Results are commonly reported as released ~July (May session) and ~January (November session) -- this release-timing pattern is widely and consistently corroborated across secondary sources but was NOT independently confirmed against a raw ibo.org results-calendar fetch this session. Flag as medium confidence pending direct verification.

H_unsafe_inferences: Do not convert an IB Diploma total (0-45) into a US GPA/4.0 value as a universal rule -- no such official conversion exists.
Do not assume a predicted grade equals the final examination result -- they are produced by different processes at different times and can diverge materially.

Do not assume a student who has IB HL/SL course grades on record has earned (or even attempted) the full IB Diploma -- the 'IB Diploma Programme courses' pathway allows individual subject participation without TOK/EE/CAS or an overall Diploma award.
Do not infer class rank from subject grades or diploma total -- IBO does not define or publish rank; it's a school-level policy matter when present at all.

Do not assume a diploma total of 24-27 points reflects the same profile strength as, say, 40+ -- both may satisfy the pass threshold but represent very different academic levels; do not treat 'awarded the Diploma' as a single flattened pass/fail signal without also surfacing the actual total and subject-level detail.

Do not assume TOK/EE letter grades (A-E) are on the same scale as, or convertible to, the 1-7 subject scale -- they are graded differently and combined via a distinct points matrix, not a shared scale.
Do not assume a school offering IB automatically offers the full 6-subject-group catalog a student would need for a given HL combination -- subject availability varies by school.
Do not treat CAS completion as a meaningful achievement/activity signal on the same footing as a subject grade -- it is a binary gate, not a graded or comparative measure of quality.

should_care_about: Which subjects were chosen at HL vs SL, and whether that selection aligns with the student's stated target field/major (e.g. HL Math + HL Physics for an Engineering target).
Trajectory between predicted grade and (once available) final grade, per subject -- a large predicted-to-final drop or rise is informative and should be surfaced, not hidden.
Whether the Diploma was pursued/awarded at all vs individual DP courses only -- materially different profile signal.
TOK and EE as evidence of independent research/argumentation skill relevant to fields valuing intellectual curiosity, distinct from subject grades.
CAS completion as evidence of sustained non-academic engagement (creativity/activity/service), read qualitatively rather than as a score.
should_not_care_about: Fabricating a GPA-equivalent number from the diploma total.
Computing or displaying an inferred class rank.
Treating 'Diploma awarded: yes' alone as sufficient -- must retain subject-level and core-element detail.
Assuming grade boundary percentages that don't exist as a fixed table.

J_profile_data_model_implications.fits_existing_schema_how: education_records.curriculum='ib' is a reasonable base tag for a DP (or DP-courses-only) enrollment period. The 6 subjects map cleanly to 6 courses rows with level='ib_hl' or level='ib_sl', subject/course_name populated per subject, academic_year set. This part of the existing design is sound.
gaps: PREDICTED vs FINAL grade: courses.grade_value is a single TEXT field with no accompanying 'assessment status' (predicted / final / mock). A DP subject legitimately has (at minimum) a predicted grade at application time and a different final grade after results -- today's schema can only hold one grade_value per course row at a time, forcing either an overwrite (losing the predicted value once final arrives, which destroys the trajectory signal counselors should care about per section I) or a hacky duplicate-row workaround (two courses rows with the same course_name/academic_year distinguished only by notes, which is fragile and not queryable). This is a REAL, confirmed gap -- recommend either an explicit grade_status enum column on courses (e.g. predicted/final/mock) or a separate ib_predicted_grades-style side table.

TOK and EE: courses.level enum currently only has 'ib_hl'/'ib_sl' (plus the generic non-IB values) -- there is no level value for TOK or EE, and forcing them in as a 'course' row is semantically awkward since they aren't one of the 6 subject-group subjects, use an A-E scale instead of 1-7, credit_hours doesn't really apply the same way, and their combined 0-3 point contribution comes from a joint matrix rather than an independent per-subject score. This is a genuine gap: either extend the level enum (e.g. add 'ib_tok', 'ib_ee') and accept the A-E-vs-1-7 scale mismatch inside grade_value/grade_scale (workable if grade_scale is stored as free text like 'A-E'), or model DP-core elements in a small dedicated table. Recommend flagging to the schema owner rather than silently forcing TOK/EE into courses today.

CAS: has no clean home at all. It is not a course (no grade), not a test_score (not a test), and the existing activities-style tables (per PRODUCT_SPEC, not directly inspected in this research task) would need a special 'CAS-certified: yes/no' flag plus the 7 IBO learning outcomes to be faithfully represented -- otherwise CAS entries would look like ordinary self-reported activities with no way to represent the diploma-gating completion certification. Confirmed gap, unresolved -- needs a product decision, not something this research task should force a specific design for.

IB Diploma total (0-45): repurposing education_records.overall_gpa/gpa_scale to store it (e.g. overall_gpa=38, gpa_scale=45) is technically possible but SEMANTICALLY WRONG and risky: gpa_scale/overall_gpa fields elsewhere in the product are treated as GPA-shaped values (the existing product rule in lib/requirements/evaluate.ts already says GPA is never cross-converted between scales -- but that rule assumes the field genuinely holds a GPA-like linear achievement proxy). The IB total is a bounded composite with its OWN pass/fail gating logic (24-point threshold plus the 6 failing conditions in section B) that doesn't behave like a GPA at all -- e.g. two students both 'passing' at 24 vs 42 look wildly different, and the threshold semantics don't map onto how GPA is normally read. Storing it in overall_gpa/gpa_scale invites future code (anything that averages, sorts, or displays 'GPA' generically) to mishandle it. Recommend a dedicated field (e.g. diploma_points_total / diploma_points_max=45) rather than repurposing the GPA fields, or at minimum an explicit, enforced rule that curriculum='ib' rows must never be blended with other curricula's GPA values anywhere in scoring.

Diploma-awarded status: nothing in education_records or courses currently records whether the full Diploma was actually AWARDED (met all 9 passing conditions) vs the student merely having a set of IB course grades on file (the 'DP courses' pathway from section A). Given this is a real, sourced distinction in how IB works, its absence is a confirmed gap, not a hypothetical one.

matrix_row.curriculum_qualification_exam: Diploma Programme (curriculum) -> IB Diploma (qualification, conditional) OR individual DP course results (if Diploma not pursued/awarded) -> final examinations (May/Nov session)
matrix_row.native_grading_scale: 1-7 per subject (HL and SL alike); A-E for TOK and EE; 0-45 diploma total (derived, not a subject grade)
matrix_row.external_exam: Yes -- externally set and/or externally moderated per subject, May or November session
matrix_row.predicted_grades: Yes, formal and university-facing (esp. via UCAS in the UK) -- teacher/school professional judgment, not IBO-calculated, not a guarantee of final result
matrix_row.course_levels: Higher Level (HL, 3-4 of 6 subjects) and Standard Level (SL, remaining subjects); same 1-7 scale for both
matrix_row.class_rank_inherent: No -- not defined or published by IBO; if present at all, it is a school/national-system policy layered on top

A_identity.owner_authority: College Board, a US non-profit membership organization. Administered via multiple official properties: apstudents.collegeboard.org (student-facing), apcentral.collegeboard.org (educator/coordinator-facing), international.collegeboard.org (international-school-facing).
A_identity.countries_contexts: Originates in and is predominantly associated with the United States (secondary/high school context, typically grades 9-12), but is also administered at authorized schools internationally -- the existence of a dedicated international.collegeboard.org portal, directly fetched in this research, confirms AP is administered outside the US at authorized international schools, not purely a domestic US program. No fixed minimum/maximum age is defined by College Board for the exam itself (self-study/independent candidates are explicitly permitted, see below).
A_identity.qualification_type: AP is NOT a diploma and is not, by itself, a whole curriculum. It is precisely three separate concepts that ORYN must not conflate: (1) an 'AP course' -- a year-long class taught at the student's own school (or via an authorized online provider, or via self-study) that follows a College Board-published course framework/description; the course only carries the 'AP' label on an official transcript if the school's specific course section was authorized through the College Board's AP Course Audit and appears on that school's 'AP Course Ledger' entry (directly confirmed via WebFetch of international.collegeboard.org, see sources) -- so a teacher informally calling a class 'AP' without Ledger authorization is a real, if edge-case, gap between label and College-Board-recognized status; (2) the 'AP Exam' -- the standardized assessment, externally authored and scored by College Board, administered in a fixed May window, independent of how (or whether) the student was taught the material; (3) the 'AP Exam score' -- the 1-5 result of that exam. There is no general 'AP diploma.' The one narrow exception is the 'AP Capstone Diploma' -- a distinct, optional, additional recognition (not a replacement for a school's actual high-school diploma) requiring scores of 3+ on both AP Seminar and AP Research plus 4 additional AP exams of the student's choosing (also scored 3+); scoring 3+ on just Seminar+Research alone yields a lesser 'AP Seminar and Research Certificate' instead. There is also a family of 'AP Scholar' awards (AP Scholar, AP Scholar with Honor, and further tiers) issued by College Board based on patterns of exam scores across multiple exams -- these are College-Board-issued recognitions layered on top of exam performance, not a curriculum or diploma.

J_profile_data_model_implications.core_finding_curriculum_vs_course_level: AP is NEVER properly a whole education_records.curriculum value, and having 'ap' as a peer enum option alongside 'ib' / 'a_level' / 'turkish_curriculum' / 'national_curriculum' / 'other' is a genuine concept-flattening error in the current schema, confirmed by this research rather than assumed. Reasoning: IB DP, A-Level, and a national curriculum are all SCHOOL-WIDE curricular frameworks that a student is enrolled IN for an entire stage of schooling (a school 'is' or 'is not' an IB World School running the DP; a UK school 'runs' A-Levels). AP has no equivalent whole-school-framework meaning -- there is no 'AP curriculum' a student's entire schooling follows, no 'AP diploma' that stands in for a high-school diploma (AP Capstone Diploma is an optional supplementary recognition, not a replacement for the school's own graduation credential -- see A), and no concept of a school 'being an AP school' the way it can 'be an IB World School.' Virtually ANY school running almost ANY base curriculum (a standard US school on 'national_curriculum,' a Turkish school on 'turkish_curriculum,' even in principle an IB or A-Level school) can ALSO offer some number of AP courses as an enrichment layer alongside its real underlying curriculum. So curriculum='ap' invites a student's base education_records row to be mis-tagged with a course-level enrichment label instead of their actual school-wide framework -- exactly the flattening error the research brief warned about.
J_profile_data_model_implications.recommended_fit: An AP course belongs as a courses row with level='ap' (course_name e.g. 'AP Calculus BC', subject='Mathematics'), nested under an education_records row whose curriculum field describes the student's ACTUAL base schooling framework (e.g. 'national_curriculum' for a typical US school, or 'other' if no better enum fit exists for a de-centralized US-style system) -- NOT curriculum='ap'. This part of courses.level is already correctly designed; the problem is specifically that education_records.curriculum offers 'ap' as if it were a peer concept to 'ib'/'a_level', when it structurally is not. Recommend either removing 'ap' from the education_records.curriculum enum, or restricting its legitimate use to a narrow, deliberately-scoped edge case (e.g. a supplementary record type for a self-study/independent AP candidate not tied to any normal school enrollment) that the product team should decide on explicitly rather than leave to default enum availability.
J_profile_data_model_implications.ap_exam_score_placement: The AP EXAM SCORE correctly belongs in test_scores (test_name='AP Calculus BC', score='5', max_score='5'), separate from the AP COURSE GRADE which correctly belongs in the corresponding courses row's grade_value. This split is assessed as CORRECT and is a genuine strength of the current schema: it faithfully mirrors the real-world independence of course grade (school-controlled) and exam score (College-Board-controlled) established in sections B/C -- unlike the curriculum-level 'ap' problem above, this course-vs-test_scores split does not need to change.

B_grading_model.current_official_scale: A*-G letter grades (A* highest, G lowest reported pass grade, U = ungraded/fail) is Cambridge's primary and currently reaffirmed grading scale for Cambridge IGCSE.
B_grading_model.numeric_9_1_nuance: A 9-1 numeric grading option exists as an ALTERNATIVE scale that some schools/regions have been able to choose since June 2019 (historically described for 'Administration Zone 3' schools), reported for CERTAIN subjects. However, Cambridge's own most recent factsheet (dated 2025) states plainly and without regional qualification: 'Cambridge IGCSE is graded A*-G... Are Cambridge still using A*-G grading? Yes.' This 2025 document does not mention a 9-1 option at all, suggesting A*-G is the current default/standard answer, while any 9-1 option is a narrower, region/subject-specific variant rather than the primary system. IMPORTANT: this is a genuinely two-layered fact -- do not report only 'A*-G' or only '9-1' as if the other doesn't exist.
B_grading_model.important_distinction_vs_uk_domestic_gcs: The 9-1 scale was introduced by the UK GOVERNMENT for domestic GCSEs taken in state schools in ENGLAND specifically (from August 2017) -- this is a DIFFERENT qualification (UK domestic GCSE, e.g. via AQA/Edexcel/OCR for England) from Cambridge's own IGCSE. Cambridge's official messaging frames itself as retaining A*-G by popular demand from its schools, explicitly contrasting this with the English government's own 9-1 reform of domestic GCSEs. Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland do NOT use 9-1 for their domestic GCSEs either.
B_grading_model.equivalence_anchor_points: Cambridge's own published crosswalk (2025 factsheet) shows three 'anchor points' between the scales: A*=9/8/7, (B/C)=6/5/4, (D/E/F/G)=3/2/1, U=U. This is Cambridge's OWN published equivalence for comparing grade sets when both exist -- it is not an invented conversion. Even so, it is a grade-set equivalence, not a GPA conversion, and should not be used to derive a numeric GPA.
B_grading_model.pass_fail: G (A*-G scale) or grade 1 (9-1 scale) is the lowest passing grade; below that is 'U' (ungraded), which is not a fail letter grade -- there is no F equivalent.
B_grading_model.gpa_conversion: NONE found. No authoritative Cambridge source provides an official IGCSE-to-4.0-GPA conversion for any stated purpose. Any such conversion seen elsewhere (counselor blogs, third-party tools) is NOT Cambridge-sourced and must not be treated as authoritative.

B_grading_model.a_level_scale: A* (highest) to E (minimum passing grade), reported as uppercase letters; below E is 'Ungraded' (U) -- there is no F-equivalent fail letter.
B_grading_model.as_level_scale: a to e (lowercase letters on official documents), with NO A* available at AS Level -- the ceiling grade at AS is 'a', not 'A*'. Below e is Ungraded (U).
B_grading_model.percentage_uniform_mark_pum: For some countries, Cambridge also issues a Percentage Uniform Mark (PUM), a 0-100 numeric mark on a common scale showing where within a grade band a candidate performed (e.g. PUM 79 = top of a B grade). PUM bands are officially published: A Level A*=90-100, A=80-89, B=70-79, C=60-69, D=50-59, E=40-49; AS Level a=80-100, b=70-79, c=60-69, d=50-59, e=40-49. PUM is a per-subject numeric mark, NOT a GPA and NOT an aggregate across subjects.
B_grading_model.no_gpa_calculated: Cambridge's own official 'guide for universities' states explicitly: 'Each subject is graded separately and no Grade Point Average is calculated.' This is a direct, authoritative, sourced confirmation that Cambridge itself does not compute or endorse any GPA for AS/A Level results.
B_grading_model.gpa_conversion: NONE officially provided by Cambridge for AS/A Level results either. A separate Cambridge document (Cambridge International AS & A Level Grading Scale PDF, framed for a US audience) gives a rough LETTER-GRADE comparison to US high-school letter grades (e.g. A Level A maps to roughly 'A' US letter grade, A Level E maps to roughly 'C' US letter grade) for general orientation purposes -- but this is explicitly a letter-to-letter comparison, NOT a 4.0 GPA conversion, and Cambridge does not provide numeric GPA equivalents. Do not extend this letter comparison into a numeric GPA without a separately sourced, explicit conversion table.

C_structure_concepts.as_level_standalone_or_first_half: BOTH, depending on the route chosen -- and this is explicitly documented by Cambridge as three distinct options, which is the single most important structural fact for this qualification: (1) 'Standalone AS' -- a student takes the Cambridge International AS Level ONLY, as a complete, final qualification in its own right (syllabus content is half of the full A Level programme); (2) 'AS as first half of A Level (staged/linear-staged assessment)' -- a student takes the AS Level in Year 1 (which is ALSO separately certificated at that point) and then completes the remaining A Level content in Year 2, with the AS mark able to be carried forward into the final A Level grade (carry-forward allowed twice within a 13-month period; NOT possible in all subjects, notably language syllabuses); (3) 'Full/linear A Level' -- a student takes all papers of the A Level course in the same examination series, usually at the end of the second year, without a separate AS certification along the way.
C_structure_concepts.important_precision_note: This researched answer is specifically for CAMBRIDGE INTERNATIONAL AS & A Level. UK-domestic AS Level (as administered by English exam boards for schools in England) was DECOUPLED from A Level by the 2015-2017 UK linear reform, becoming a fully standalone qualification that (in England) generally no longer counts toward the A Level grade at all. Cambridge International's system, per its own 2018 'guide for universities', still explicitly supports the CARRY-FORWARD staged route (AS marks counting toward the full A Level) as one of three official options -- this is a genuine structural difference between 'UK domestic A Level' and 'Cambridge International A Level' that ORYN must not conflate. (Given the source is dated 2018, a school's current policy for a given syllabus/session should still be confirmed against the live grade-threshold pages if precision for a specific student's session is required.)
C_structure_concepts.aice_diploma_exists: An OPTIONAL aggregate credential called the Cambridge AICE Diploma DOES exist -- a group certificate awarded for passing exams in subjects drawn from three curriculum areas (mathematics & science, languages, arts & humanities) within Cambridge International AS & A Level. Each AS Level = 1 credit, each full A Level = 2 credits; minimum 7 credits required (including the compulsory AS in Global Perspectives & Research, since 2017). Cambridge states the AICE Diploma 'is taken primarily in the USA'. This means A Level DOES have an optional holistic/aggregate layer (unlike IGCSE, which has none) -- ORYN should not assume 'no holistic option exists at all' for A Level; it should assume no holistic score is present UNLESS a student's record specifically indicates AICE Diploma participation.
C_structure_concepts.exam_sessions: Two main examination series per year: May/June and October/November (the AS/A Level guide for universities references a 'June 2018' series example; general Cambridge scheduling pattern for Cambridge Advanced is the same twice-yearly cadence as IGCSE).
C_structure_concepts.subject_load: Per Cambridge's own guide (2018): students 'typically study four subjects at AS Level and three subjects at A Level'. The standard UK-university admission requirement is stated as three A Levels. Over 50 subjects available; no compulsory subjects; schools can offer subjects in almost any combination.

sources.supports: Three-option staged/linear structure; standalone AS possible; carry-forward window of 13 months, twice; not possible for all subjects (language syllabuses excluded); exam series June/November; results August/January

E_predicted_grades.finding: Predicted grades are formally central to UCAS/UK-style university applications: UCAS itself states over 80% of university offers are conditional on predicted grades, and international-admissions guidance confirms that for international students applying with not-yet-sat exams, universities 'cannot consider your application without grade predictions'. HOWEVER, the predicted grade itself is generated by the STUDENT'S SCHOOL (teachers/heads of department, standardised by school leadership), not issued by Cambridge Assessment International Education as an official exam result. Cambridge's own official document distinguishes two related-but-different things with real precision: (1) 'PREDICTED grades' -- issued by the school to students/parents/universities for the university-application process (an external, application-process artifact); (2) 'FORECAST grades' -- the SAME underlying teacher judgement, but submitted BY THE SCHOOL TO CAMBRIDGE itself, where Cambridge uses them internally for exam-board quality-assurance purposes (deciding syllabus grade thresholds, adjusting marks for special consideration, and checks before releasing results) -- this second use IS a genuine Cambridge exam-board process, but it is an internal QA input, not a grade communicated to students as 'their predicted grade' in the university-application sense. Cambridge International schools OUTSIDE the UK still generate predicted grades for their own students' use in applications (UCAS or otherwise) -- this is a school-level practice enabled/guided by Cambridge (Cambridge publishes a 'Predicted grades: a guide for schools' document to help schools do this fairly), but the FORMAL REQUIREMENT to submit a predicted grade as part of an application is a UCAS/university-process convention layered on top of the Cambridge qualification, not an intrinsic deliverable that Cambridge issues to the public the way a final grade is.
E_predicted_grades.staged_as_level_connection: Cambridge's own predicted-grades guidance notes that for students on the staged AS route, 'their final AS grades will count as very helpful indicators of A Level predicted grades' -- i.e., an actual (not predicted) AS result is commonly used by schools as evidence when forming an A Level prediction. This is a useful, sourced signal for ORYN: a real AS Level result can inform confidence in an A Level trajectory even before final A Level results exist.
E_predicted_grades.accuracy_caveat: External UCAS-linked reporting found in this research indicates predicted grades are frequently inaccurate -- only around 16% of predictions have been reported as exactly accurate historically, with most predictions skewing optimistic. ORYN should treat any predicted grade as a provisional estimate, never as a stand-in for a final result.

gaps: REAL GAP: courses.level has no distinct value for a STANDALONE or STAGED AS Level result, separate from a full 'a_level'. Since the assignment's own unsafe-inference rule (and Cambridge's own guide-for-universities examples, e.g. University of Sydney not accepting AS in place of A Level) establishes that AS Level and full A Level are NOT equivalent evidence, forcing an AS Level course into level='a_level' would misrepresent its depth/weight. REAL GAP (shared with the parallel IB/AP predicted-vs-final investigation): there is no field anywhere in education_records or courses to mark a grade_value as PREDICTED/FORECAST vs FINAL. Cambridge's own materials draw a sharp, sourced line between predicted grades (school estimate, pre-exam, used for applications) and final grades (Cambridge-issued, post-exam, official) -- these are epistemically different kinds of evidence (self/school-reported estimate vs. externally verified official result) and the schema's evidence-integrity principle (never present self-reported as verified) argues for NOT storing them interchangeably in the same untyped grade_value TEXT field. Recommend either a grade_status/grade_type field (e.g. predicted|forecast|final) on courses, or routing predicted grades through a clearly-labeled mechanism separate from final grade_value -- this is the same finding the IB/AP researcher was independently asked to check, and for Cambridge specifically the answer is: yes, this is a real, sourced gap, not a hypothetical one.

The Percentage Uniform Mark (PUM), where available, is a natural fit for test_scores.subscores (jsonb) if AS/A Level results are modeled as test_scores rather than (or in addition to) courses -- worth a deliberate decision on which table is canonical for Cambridge exam results, since they are externally-set/marked exams (arguably closer to 'test_scores' in spirit) rather than school-internal coursework (which 'courses.grade_value' seems designed around).
